Core Capability Areas
Why Now

Three forces are converging on the trust layer.

Post-quantum standards, AI-agent adoption and API-driven services are no longer separate roadmaps — they're hitting regulated enterprises at the same time.

01

PQC has moved into implementation

NIST has finalised three post-quantum standards and is encouraging administrators to begin transition planning now, because full integration takes years to get right.

02

AI agents are becoming action systems

Security has to cover agents, MCP servers and tools directly — and the APIs that turn AI output into real enterprise action, not just advice.

03

Data and keys are moving everywhere

Hybrid cloud, AI, analytics and SaaS all need one consistent approach to key governance, tokenisation and data protection — not five different ones.

How It Connects

One trust layer. Six places it breaks.

Every regulated enterprise runs on a hidden trust layer spanning identities, APIs, AI agents, cryptography and data across cloud and infrastructure. TrustFabric secures that layer end to end.

  • APIsShadow endpoints, sensitive data flows and business logic abuse.
  • AI AgentsAgents and tools acting on systems without enough governance.
  • CryptoAlgorithms, certificates, HSMs, keys and cryptographic lifecycle control.
  • IdentityHuman and machine identities with excessive, unmanaged or persistent access.
  • DataClassification, residency and protection across every workload.
  • PQCMigration roadmap, crypto-agility and quantum-safe transition.
